subject: COURSE NAME
title: Round N
notes: Short pack subtitle, max 120 chars — shown under the pack title on the course card.

questions._comment: MULTIPLE CHOICE — use for direct recall, single-concept distinction
questions.explanation: The correct answer is right because <reason>. Distractor A is wrong because <reason>; distractor B confuses this with <other concept>; distractor C applies only when <condition>.

questions._comment: MULTIPLE CHOICE (misconception) — `true_false` is REJECTED by L26. Test a textbook trap by making the misconception a distractor instead of a coin-flip.
questions.explanation: The accurate statement is correct because <reason>. The common misconception fails because <reason>; the related-but-wrong statement describes <other concept>; the plausible-sounding invention is not a real behavior.

questions._comment: MULTIPLE SELECT (term/definition) — `matching` is REJECTED by L26. Cover term/definition breadth by asking which descriptions fit one term, one question per term.
questions.prompt: Which of the following describe <Term A>? (Select all that apply.)
options: A true property of Term A
A property of Term B, not Term A
Another true property of Term A
A property of Term C, not Term A
questions.explanation: Both keyed properties belong to Term A because <reason>. The distractors are true of Term B and Term C respectively, not Term A.

questions._comment: SCENARIO MULTIPLE CHOICE — use for applied concepts, normalization problems
questions.prompt: An organization discovers <condition> while <activity> is already in progress, and <constraint> rules out the obvious response. What is the best approach?
questions.explanation: This approach works because <reason>. Common mistake A fails because <reason>; common mistake B addresses a different problem; the unrelated approach does not apply to this scenario at all.

questions._comment: MULTIPLE SELECT — use for 'select all that apply', multi-fact recall. `answers` lists ALL correct indices; grading is all-or-nothing.
questions.prompt: A team needs <outcome>. Which measures achieve it? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Why the two correct options apply and why the distractors do not.
